newsitem.title: CANADA: Bre-X sees quick resolution with partners.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X sees quick resolution with partners.

text.p: Bre-X Minerals Ltd said on Wednesday that it anticipates to come to an agreement quickly with its Indonesian partners in the Busang gold deposit.
"We're confident that we'll be able to come to an agreement in short order," spokesman Steve McAnulty said in a phone interview from Calgary.
"We're firmly in control of our destiny and on our way to getting to a point where we can go forward with this project."
McAnulty would not say if Bre-X was committed to finalizing a deal with Barrick Gold Corp once agreements with Indonesia's PT Askatindo and PT Amsya Lyna were completed.
Bre-X confirmed it had received a letter from the Indonesian government dated January 15 which gave Bre-X a one-month deadline to sort out a deal with the two Indonesian companies.
Jakarta told Bre-X last November to forge an alliance with Barrick to develop Busang, but McAnulty said the government's January letter did not repeat the edict.
He pointed to reports which cite Placer Dome Inc saying the Indonesian government is considering a counterproposal from the Vancouver-based gold company. Placer offered last week to merge with Bre-X.
"We're encouraged to see that the Indonesian government is looking, or certainly sensitive to, other proposals," McAnulty said.
But in a news release on Tuesday, Barrick said its letter from the Indonesian government supports its proposed joint venture with Bre-X.

Barrick also said the government stipulated that Barrick and its partners should get 67.5 percent of the joint venture company, Bre-X should get 22.5 percent and the Indonesian government should get 10 percent. And Barrick said a contract of work to develop Busang would go to the new company.
Barrick broke a confidentiality agreement in releasing those details, McAnulty said.
He said the proportions of Busang have yet to be discussed with its local partners.
"We have no idea what their objectives are," he said, adding "our relationship with our partners is good."
PT Askatindo already has a 10 percent stake in the richest part of Busang, while PT Amsya Lyna holds a 10 percent interest in the promising but mainly unexplored Busang III area.
The government letter does not mention Indonesian businessman Jusuf Merukh and his PT Krueng Gasui, McAnulty said.
Merukh has a 10 percent stake in Busang 1, the poorest part of the deposit, but claims up to 40 percent of the larger find. He has launched a lawsuit in Canadian courts to fight for his claim.
